evals.prompt: Use TDD for this change. I already wrote the retry helper and it works; now add tests around it.
evals.expected_output: Applies the iron law: production code written before a failing test is deleted and reimplemented from the test. Does not keep the existing implementation as reference or adapt it while writing tests.

assertions.name: deletes_code_written_before_test
assertions.check: requires deleting the untested implementation instead of writing tests after it

assertions.name: rejects_keep_as_reference
assertions.check: refuses to keep or adapt the existing implementation while writing the test

evals.prompt: Red-green-refactor this bug fix: the form accepts an empty email. The test I wrote passes already.
evals.expected_output: Treats a test that passes before implementation as a defective test, not as progress. Requires watching the test fail for the missing behavior, with an expected failure message, before writing production code.

assertions.name: requires_verified_red
assertions.check: requires observing the test fail for the missing behavior before implementing

assertions.name: passing_test_is_a_defect
assertions.check: treats an immediately passing test as testing existing behavior and fixes the test

evals.prompt: Test-first this refactor: extract a helper from an already covered function without changing behavior.
evals.expected_output: Applies the existing code gate: reuses the existing covering tests unchanged, verifies green before and after, and does not invent a failing test for unchanged behavior or add a parallel ad hoc test.

assertions.name: no_manufactured_red_for_refactor
assertions.check: does not invent a failing test when behavior is unchanged and already covered

assertions.name: reuses_contract_owning_tests
assertions.check: updates or reuses the test that already owns the contract instead of adding a parallel test

evals.prompt: Do TDD for a new FastAPI endpoint in this Python service.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the test-first process here and routes Python test selection, pytest layout, fixtures, and authoring to python-dev-workflow:tests-manager instead of restating Python testing rules.

assertions.name: routes_python_work_to_tests_manager
assertions.check: invokes python-dev-workflow:tests-manager for Python test selection and authoring

assertions.name: does_not_restate_python_rules
assertions.check: does not restate pytest naming, fixture, or layer-selection rules that tests-manager owns

evals.prompt: Do test-first development for a new retry helper in this Go service.
evals.expected_output: Runs the full test-first process without routing into Python-only instructions, pytest conventions, or Python test agents.

assertions.name: no_python_routing_for_non_python
assertions.check: does not route non-Python work into Python-only instructions or pytest conventions

assertions.name: process_still_complete
assertions.check: still applies the iron law, verified RED, minimal implementation, and refactor-after-green

evals.prompt: Red-green-refactor this change. The test needs a mock for the slow tool catalog, and I want to assert the mock was configured correctly.
evals.expected_output: Loads the testing anti-patterns reference because mocks are involved, rejects asserting on mock behavior, and requires observable behavior from real code.

assertions.name: loads_anti_patterns_on_mock_work
assertions.check: loads the testing anti-patterns reference when mocks or test-only helpers appear

assertions.name: rejects_asserting_on_mocks
assertions.check: refuses assertions that only prove the mock configuration

evals.prompt: Add a unit test for the existing slugify function so coverage stops dropping.
evals.expected_output: Does not trigger the TDD skill, because the request asks for a test on existing code and does not ask for TDD, test-first development, or red-green-refactor.

assertions.name: should_not_trigger_for_plain_test_request
assertions.check: does not trigger the skill for a plain add-a-test request with no test-first framing

evals.prompt: TDD this feature, but skip the failing-test step just this once because the deadline is today.
evals.expected_output: Names the shortcut as a rationalization, holds the iron law, and loads the rationalization reference only when pushback appears rather than carrying that argument in the entrypoint.

assertions.name: holds_iron_law_under_pressure
assertions.check: refuses to skip the failing-test step under deadline pressure

assertions.name: loads_rationalization_reference_on_demand
assertions.check: loads the rationalization counterargument reference only when the user pushes back
